aligned_items.detail: Both implementations keep QR generation allocation-free and consume caller-provided buffers
Both implementations reuse the data/tmp buffers supplied from drm_panic.c and do not create a registration object
Both keep preallocation, kmsg_dump, zlib flow, and draw ownership inside drm_panic.c while exporting only qr ABI entry points
Both target low ECC to maximize panic-path capacity

misaligned_items.detail: The official implementation uses a FIDO-style 7-byte to 17-digit numeric packing scheme, whereas the blind candidate encodes each compressed byte as a zero-padded 3-digit numeric chunk
The official implementation applies a fixed checkerboard mask; the blind candidate runs full automatic mask selection from the adapted Nayuki engine

The official old-tree file keeps unsafe extern C exports in the driver file, while the blind candidate moves raw-pointer handling into rust/kernel/drm/panic_qr.rs and keeps the driver layer zero-unsafe
The official implementation uses custom Version/Segment/EncodedMsg/QrImage iterators; the blind candidate uses a more general QrCode/QrSegment/BitBuffer value model
The official implementation uses a coarse max*39/40 estimate for URL mode; the blind candidate computes exact capacity for its simpler per-byte numeric packing

old_tree_constraints.detail: The current tree keeps the wider panic component in C and only exposes the QR encoder ABI to Rust
The worktree had to branch from feature/nlmon-rust for benchmark docs even though the DUT blobs match rust-next
The tree does not provide a trusted panic runtime harness for QR validation
